annotation.kind: source selection, explicit source-defect correction, and provisional tier review for Theorem 3.6

assumptions: The number n of product factors is positive.
The finite probability law has nonnegative masses summing to one.
Every random rounding factor 1 + delta_k is nonnegative.
Every bias beta_k satisfies |beta_k| <= B, and each beta_k after the first is determined by the preceding errors.
For every history-measurable finite test function X, E[X delta_k] = E[X beta_k].

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p17_t1_corrected_product_bias_envelope {n : Nat} {Omega : Type*} [Fintype Omega] (run : P17CorrectedProductBiasRun n Omega) : (1-run.B)^n <= p17ExpectedErrorProduct run and p17ExpectedErrorProduct run <= (1+run.B)^n
formal_statement.plain_language: Under the corrected sign conditions and Theorem 3.6's bounded conditional-bias hypotheses, the expected product of the random relative-error factors lies between the lower and upper binomial envelopes.

informal_proof: Induct on prefix length. The prefix product is nonnegative and depends only on earlier errors, so the conditional-mean identity replaces the next delta by beta inside its expectation. The bound |beta_k| <= B and expectation monotonicity place the next expectation between (1-B) and (1+B) times the preceding expectation. The explicit condition B <= 1 preserves both inequalities through the induction.
informal_statement: A project-corrected finite-probability version of Theorem 3.6's expected accumulated-product envelope, with the proof-required nonnegativity conditions made explicit.
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47(5), 2025, pages B1227-B1249

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen library supplies finite-expectation algebra and a deterministic pointwise product envelope, but no result combines bounded history-conditional biases into this expected-product theorem. The private L construction must still perform the paper-specific induction.
